title: Senior Product Manager
jd_excerpt:
Everyday Speech is a no-prep digital curriculum that makes teaching social, behavioral, and communication skills easy and effective. The MTSS-aligned curriculum combines evidence-based video modeling, interactive web games, and worksheets to provide educators everything they need to support both neurodiverse and neurotypical PK-12 students. Everyday Speech is trusted by 50,000+ special educators, speech-language pathologists, counselors, and other specialists for targeted interventions and whole-class lessons that help students build the skills they need to thrive.
 Everyday Speech is right for you if: 
 You care about making a positive impact. 
 End each day knowing your work directly impacted educators across North America in our mission to build the most impactful PreK-12 social skills curriculum and make teaching it effortless. Success goes beyond shipping features here; we’re improving the lives of educators and their students. To achieve this, we create meaningful content, stay closely connected to our users, and maintain consistently high NPS scores as a fully bootstrapped company growing organically and sustainably. 
 You value being a part of a company that takes care of its team. 
 Not only do we have extremely happy team members, we also have incredible perks. Participate in our health/wellness and retirement benefit offerings, and between having every other Friday off (3-day weekends!) and our flexible PTO plan, that elusive work-life balance is an actual thing here. We’ve also never had an office and never will. We take remote work seriously and know how to support a distributed team. We give you the flexibility to work in a way that’s best for you, but still have high standards and accountability. These are just some of the reasons why our eNPS score from 2025 was 78.
 You want to be at a company whose values are more than just words on a wall. 
 Our values are at the forefront of our decisions, how we recognize each other, how we challenge ourselves— everything we do. Our values mean something, and with that guiding light, we are able to land with clarity, create alignment, identify our strengths, and move with purpose. Hear it directly from a team member: “I love the values. I never imagined I could end up in a position that was so connected to the things that mattered to me most”. 
 As a member of the Product Design & Management team, the Senior Product Manager will translate company strategy into concrete improvements for our go-to-market teams: more efficient workflows and tooling, and new systems that accelerate growth. You’ll partner with GTM teams and the owners of their tools, including HubSpot, Maxio, and our product platform, to decide what gets built, who builds it, and how it gets adopted. Because the same licensing, access, and usage data serves both our GTM teams and our customer admins, you’ll also lead product work on the customer admin experience, so districts and schools can license, access, and manage Everyday Speech on their own. Across both, you’ll leverage data to make decisions and help GTM teams and admins do the same.
 We treat our go-to-market motion as a second product, and we intend to make it best in class. Every hour we give back to a rep goes into a district conversation. Every access issue we remove before back-to-school gets an educator teaching sooner. You'll use AI to change how our Sales, CS, and Billing teams work, building some of it yourself with tools like Claude Code and leading bigger bets through our Shape Up cycles.
 This is a fully remote position. This role will be required to work Eastern or Central time zone hours, approximately 9:00 am - 5:00 pm ET.
 The ideal candidate is extremely values aligned :
 ● We start with empathy — in the work we do and the people we do it with. Our strength comes from a culture that values candidness, trust, and valuing our teammates as whole human beings. We care, challenge, and communicate. We are serious about our responsibility to educators, who rely on us every day.
 ● We ruthlessly prioritize. We don ’t just say no to the obvious stuff, we say no to the things that feel important in the moment because we understand anything we say yes to is inherently saying no to something else.
 ● We create momentum. We don’t let the small stuff hold us back. We learn by shipping. We know most actions are reversible and that action always wins in the long run. If all else fails, bias towards action.
 ● We are fearlessly objective. We don't do things just because we're "supposed to." We constantly ask "why" and don’t let conventional norms define our efforts. We're not afraid to seek answers, even if that means discovering we were wrong. We focus on what delivers results, regardless of the source.
 ● We exercise agency. We have the ability to create systems that don’t yet exist to get what we need or to solve problems no one has identified. If something isn’t working, it’s within our control to fix it.
 ● We’re driven to grow. We set ambitious goals because we want to maximize our impact. We embrace challenges and take risks, seeing failures as opportunities to learn and improve. We seek out feedback and coaching and thrive in environments that push us.

 In this role, you will: 
 Build the product that powers how we grow. Our GTM systems are as critical as our curriculum product, and our GTM teams are your primary users. Learn their workflows, strategy, and pain points well enough to see what they can't, and let that drive what gets built and how it rolls out.
 Decide what matters most, and bring people with you. Own the GTM build backlog. Turn a stream of requests into a few initiatives that solve problems at the root, make the trade-off calls, and get GTM leaders and frontline teams behind the plan.
 Ask the question no one else is asking. Probe past the request to the ground truth of the problem. Challenge assumptions, question how things have always been done, and push back when existing systems or processes don't serve what teams actually need.
 Turn hard, cross-system problems into bets that ship. Shape multi-team, multi-system work for our six-week Shape Up cycles, then run it: sequencing, owners, dates, risks, and rollout timing. Partner with RevOps, Billing Ops, and Engineering so changes across HubSpot, Maxio, and our product platform fit together, don't break downstream workflows, and keep data consistent.
 Ship with AI, don't just spec it. Use tools like Claude Code to prototype, automate workflows, and ship fixes yourself. Know when a problem is big enough to hand to engineering, and write specs precise enough for them to build from.
 Change how people work, not just the tools they have. Lead rollout and enablement so the teams you build for actually adopt what you ship, then use their feedback to decide what comes next.
 Clear the path from contract to classroom. Lead the customer admin experience and make district setup effortless: licensing, access, user management, rostering, SSO, and onboarding. Design shared data to serve admins and internal teams at once, and be the product voice on district calls.
 Prove the impact. Make usage data a standard part of onboarding, renewal, and expansion conversations, and track the metrics that show how your work enables GTM teams to spend more time with customers.
 What We’re Looking For 
 In addition to values alignment…
 5+ years of experience in product management, platform product management, or business systems product management, operating independently across a company-wide scope
 Prioritization and consensus building: you align senior stakeholders with competing priorities, make trade-off calls, and defend them
 Exceptional project management skills: you bring order to work spanning many stakeholders and interconnected systems
 Systems thinking: hands-on experience with CRM, billing, licensing, or entitlements systems, and a habit of anticipating downstream effects
 Technical fluency: you read API docs, data models, and architecture diagrams, and understand how systems integrate and how data maps between them
 AI building: comfortable using AI development tools (Claude Code or similar) to prototype and ship small internal tools, or a clear aptitude and drive to learn, plus the judgment to know when to build yourself and when to hand it off
 Clear written communication, including specs with precise business rules and edge cases
 Strongly preferred: 
 Experience as a PM for GTM systems or internal tools
 HubSpot or similar CRM architecture knowledge
 Experience applying AI or LLMs to operational workflows
 Data fluency: comfortable defining metrics and pulling your own answers
 Frontline empathy, ideally from a Customer Success, Account Management, or Sales background
 EdTech experience, or SaaS experience with an appetite to learn school buying cycles, annual contracts, and pilot timing
 Nice to have: 
 K-12 rostering and SSO experience (Clever, ClassLink)
 Clear technical communication with district IT teams
 Student data privacy knowledge
 RevOps, solutions engineering, or implementation background
 We know great candidates come from a wide range of backgrounds. If you’re passionate about what we’re building at Everyday Speech , don’t hesitate to apply, even if you’re not sure you meet every qualification. 
 In your first 90 days, you will: 
 Ship a win in your first 30 days. Find a manual task that costs a frontline team hours every week, and remove it with AI tools or a quick fix.
 Learn the work from the inside. Shadow CS, AM, Sales, Support, and Billing Operations, map where manual work and handoffs slow them down, and turn what you see into your next few wins.
 Learn our systems end to end. Get to know HubSpot, Maxio, our product platform, the Admin Portal, and Account Hub, including how data flows between them.
 Bring order to the backlog. Consolidate open GTM requests into a single prioritized backlog that GTM leaders agree on.
 Put your first cross-system bet on the table. Shape at least one initiative for an upcoming Shape Up betting cycle.
 Set your baselines. Establish the metrics you'll be measured against, so your impact is visible from the start.
 In your first year, you will: 
 Give GTM teams their time back. Measurably cut the time they spend updating systems and doing admin work, so more of their day goes to customer conversations.
 Make new revenue motions a matter of weeks, not months. 
 Deliver multi-system initiatives on time, without breaking downstream workflows, on data that stays clean and consistent across HubSpot, Maxio, and our platform.
 Build tools teams choose to use. See high adoption among the teams you build for.
 Let districts get up and running on their own. Admins self-serve onboarding, user management, and access; time from signed contract to active users drops; and access tickets fall, especially at back-to-school.
 Renewal and expansion conversations run on usage data. 
 Salary : $134,565 USD annually, plus company performance-based bonuses, paid out twice per year, for $144,705 TCC.
 Benefits 
 ● Cigna Health Insurance – 100% premium coverage for team members & dependents
 ● Dental & Vision Coverage – 100% premium coverage for team members & dependents
 ● 3% Employer-Match on 401(k)
 ● $50K Life Insurance / AD&D
 ● Flexible PTO Plan & Sick Leave Policy
 ● 16 Weeks of Paid Parental Leave
 ● Home Office Reimbursements
 ● Book & Learning Stipend
 ● Meaningful Employee Experience Initiatives
 ● Every Other Friday Off After 90 Days!
 Explore our candidate site to learn more about what Everyday Speech does, what our work environment is like, our hiring philosophy, and more! 
 Note: Sometimes mail may land in your spam or Promotions tab. You will receive emails from @everydayspeech.com or . Be sure to keep us in your primary inbox so you don't miss a message!
